title: Golden rosemary roast chicken
description: Crisp golden skin, garlic pan juices and rosemary potatoes. A Sunday roast worth gathering around.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C. Pat the chicken dry and rub with the butter and half the salt. Put the lemon and one rosemary sprig inside the cavity.
Toss the potatoes and garlic with the oil, remaining salt and rosemary in a roasting tin. Set the chicken on top.
Roast for about 90 minutes, turning the potatoes halfway through. Check with a thermometer that the thickest breast and thigh reach at least 74°C, away from the bone. Continue cooking if needed.
Transfer the chicken to a board and rest for 15 minutes. Return the potatoes to the oven to crisp, then serve with the pan juices.

title: Warm apple crumble tarts
description: Buttery pastry, cinnamon apples and a crisp oat crumble. Best served warm with vanilla ice cream.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C. Line six greased tart tins with pastry and prick the bases. Line with baking paper and baking beans; bake for 12 minutes, then remove the paper and beans.
Cook the apples with 20 g of the sugar, the cinnamon and 2 tbsp water over medium heat for 8 minutes, until just tender.
Rub the butter into the flour until crumbly, then stir in the oats and remaining sugar. Divide the apples between the pastry cases and scatter the crumble over them.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until the pastry and topping are golden. Cool for 15 minutes before serving.

title: Bubbling beef lasagna
description: Rich tomato ragù, creamy béchamel and a bubbling golden cheese crust. Save a corner piece.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a deep pan. Soften the onion for 8 minutes, add the garlic, then brown the beef thoroughly, breaking it up with a spoon.
Add the tomatoes, season to taste and simmer for 25 minutes. Heat the oven to 190°C.
Layer the ragù, pasta sheets and béchamel in a baking dish, finishing with béchamel and both cheeses. Follow the pasta packet instructions if the sheets need precooking.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until the pasta is tender, the centre is piping hot and the top is golden. Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Lemon pea and mint pasta
description: Sweet green peas, ribbons of lemon zest and fresh mint in a silky parmesan sauce.

steps.text: Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil. Cook the pasta according to the packet instructions, adding the peas for the final 3 minutes.
Reserve a mug of pasta water, then drain. Return the pasta and peas to the warm pan off the heat.
Toss with the butter, lemon zest, half the lemon juice and parmesan. Add a little pasta water at a time until the sauce coats the pasta.
Fold in the mint, taste and add more lemon juice, salt and pepper as needed. Serve straight away.

title: Strawberry cream tart
description: A crisp pastry shell, vanilla cream and juicy strawberries. A little sunshine on a plate.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C. Line a 23 cm tart tin with the pastry and prick the base. Line with baking paper and baking beans.
Bake for 15 minutes. Remove the paper and beans and bake for 10 minutes more, until golden and cooked through. Cool completely for about 45 minutes.
Whisk the mascarpone, cream, icing sugar and vanilla until thick enough to hold soft peaks.
Spoon the cream into the cooled shell and top with strawberries. Chill for 15 minutes before slicing. Keep refrigerated and eat within 2 days.

title: Charred corn with lime butter
description: Sweetcorn blistered on the grill, brushed with chilli-lime butter and finished with coriander.

steps.text: Heat a barbecue or griddle pan to medium-high. Mix the butter with the lime zest, chilli flakes, salt and 1 tsp lime juice.
Grill the corn for 12 to 15 minutes, turning regularly, until tender with lightly charred patches.
Brush the hot corn with the lime butter. Scatter with coriander and serve with the remaining lime cut into wedges.
